cases.sentence: А еще был ___ рождения непонятно у кого.
cases.translation: And besides that, it was somebody's birthday — nobody knew whose.
cases.explain: «День рождения» is the subject of «был», and a subject stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Увидеть ее на ___, с косой от попы до затылка.
cases.translation: To see her on the platform, with her braid running from her backside to the back of her head.
cases.explain: «На» answering «где?» (a place, not a direction) requires the prepositional: на перроне.

cases.sentence: Увидеть ее на перроне и от ___ зардеться.
cases.translation: To see her on the platform and blush from excitement.
cases.explain: The preposition «от», giving the cause of a state, always governs the genitive: от волнения.

cases.translation: I was diluting the Rossiyskaya vodka with Zhiguli beer.
cases.explain: The means or substance used to do something («разбавлять чем?») goes into the instrumental, and the adjective жигулевским agrees with it.

cases.translation: She drank it standing, throwing her head back like a pianist.
cases.explain: Голова is the direct object of the transitive verbal adverb «откинув», and a direct object without negation takes the accusative.

cases.sentence: Она ___ прямо сказала: «Я хочу, чтобы ты меня властно обнял правою рукою!»
cases.translation: She told me straight out: "I want you to put your right arm around me masterfully!"
cases.explain: «Сказать» takes the addressee (the person told) in the dative, so я becomes мне.

cases.sentence: Я сижу за ___, разбавляю и пью.
cases.translation: I am sitting at the table, diluting and drinking.
cases.explain: «За» meaning 'at / behind' with a static location (сидеть где?) governs the instrumental: за столом.

reading.question: What does Venichka insist about the red-haired girl from Petushki?
options: That she is not a girl at all, but something else entirely
That she is only a girl in his imagination
That she is the youngest of the three women
That she is not from Petushki at all
reading.correct: That she is not a girl at all, but something else entirely
reading.explain: He piles up denials — she is not a girl but a ballad, not a woman but sorcery.

reading.ru: В Петушках, как я вам уже говорил, жасмин не отцветает и птичье пение не молкнет.
reading.question: How does Venichka describe Petushki?
options: The jasmine never stops blooming and the birdsong never falls silent
It is grey and empty all year round
It is louder and busier than Moscow
It smells of beer and cheap wine
reading.correct: The jasmine never stops blooming and the birdsong never falls silent
reading.explain: He repeats his earlier claim that in Petushki jasmine and birdsong never cease.

reading.ru: Вот и в этот день, ровно двенадцать недель тому назад, были птички и был жасмин.
reading.question: How long ago was the day Venichka starts to remember?
reading.explain: He dates the day of their meeting as exactly twelve weeks before the journey he is on.

reading.ru: А еще был день рождения непонятно у кого.
reading.question: What was the occasion of the gathering that day?
options: A birthday, though it was unclear whose
A holiday at the cable-laying office
reading.correct: A birthday, though it was unclear whose
reading.explain: It was somebody's birthday, but whose exactly was not clear to him.

reading.ru: И я разбавлял и пил, разбавлял российскую жигулевским пивом и глядел на этих «троих» и что-то в них прозревал.
reading.question: What did Venichka mix his Rossiyskaya vodka with while he watched the women?
reading.explain: He says plainly that he diluted the Rossiyskaya with Zhiguli beer.

reading.ru: Но вот ответное прозрение – я только в одной из них ощутил, только в одной!
reading.question: In how many of the tipsy women did Venichka feel an answering insight?
reading.explain: He stresses twice that the response came from only one of the three.

reading.question: What does the red-haired woman tell Venichka once she recognises him?
options: That she has read one of his pieces
That she has never heard of him
That she once saw him in Petushki
reading.correct: That she has read one of his pieces
reading.explain: She opens by saying she has read one little work of his.

reading.question: What is her verdict on the amount of nonsense he packed into fifty pages?
options: That it is beyond human powers
That it is not nearly enough
That it should be published at once
reading.correct: That it is beyond human powers
reading.explain: She marvels that so much drivel on half a hundred pages is more than a human being could manage — and he offers to write even more.

reading.ru: То есть началось беспамятство: три часа провала.
reading.question: What happened right after that exchange with her?
options: A three-hour blackout he cannot remember
He left the party and went home
He fell asleep on the platform
reading.correct: A three-hour blackout he cannot remember
reading.explain: Everything began with a gap of three hours he cannot account for — what he drank, what he said, in what proportion he diluted.

reading.question: What did Venichka find when he came round three hours later?
options: Nobody was left but the two of them
The whole company was still drinking
He was alone in the room
He was already on the train
reading.correct: Nobody was left but the two of them
reading.explain: He wakes at the table to find only himself and her, still laughing at him.

reading.ru: Стоя выпила, откинув голову, как пианистка.
reading.question: How does Venichka describe the way she drank her extra hundred grams?
options: Standing up, head thrown back, like a pianist
Sitting down, without looking at him
reading.correct: Standing up, head thrown back, like a pianist
reading.explain: The comparison he uses for her posture as she drinks is a pianist.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what he wants to do when he first sees her on the platform?
sentences: Но сначала все-таки к ней.
Сначала – к ней!
Увидеть ее на перроне, с косой от попы до затылка, и от волнения зардеться, и вспыхнуть, и напиться влежку, и пастись, пастись между лилиями – ровно столько, чтобы до смерти изнемочь!
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence goes beyond 'to her first' and spells out the meeting on the platform.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how much drink there was at the party?
sentences: В Петушках, как я вам уже говорил, жасмин не отцветает и птичье пение не молкнет.
Вот и в этот день, ровно двенадцать недель тому назад, были птички и был жасмин.
А еще был день рождения непонятно у кого.
И еще – была бездна всякого спиртного: не то десять бутылок, не то двенадцать, не то двадцать пять.
И было все, что может пожелать человек, выпивший столько спиртного: то есть решительно все, от разливного пива до бутылочного.
«А еще? – спросите вы. – А еще что было?»
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence counts the bottles — ten, or twelve, or twenty-five.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what position he found himself in when he came to?
sentences: Вот – с этого все началось.
То есть началось беспамятство: три часа провала.
Что я пил?
О чем говорил?
В какой пропорции разбавлял?
Может, этого провала и не было бы, если б я пил, не разбавляя.
Но – как бы то ни было – я очнулся часа через три, и вот в каком положении я очнулся: я сижу за столом, разбавляю и пью.
highlight.explain: The last sentence answers it: he came round at the table, still diluting and drinking.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the way she stood as she drank?
sentences: А она взяла – и выпила еще сто грамм.
Стоя выпила, откинув голову, как пианистка.
А выпив, все из себя выдохнула, все, что в ней было святого, – все выдохнула.
А потом изогнулась, как падла, и начала волнообразные движения бедрами, – и все это с такою пластикою, что я не мог глядеть на нее без содрогания…
highlight.explain: The second sentence gives her posture — standing, head thrown back like a pianist.
